explanation: Ibn Sina, known in Latin as Avicenna, finished it around 1025. Rhazes, another Persian physician, wrote earlier works that Europeans also studied.

claims.text: Avicenna (Ibn Sina), a Persian scholar, wrote The Canon of Medicine.
Latin translations of The Canon of Medicine were used in European universities for centuries.
Averroes, Rhazes and Alhazen did not write The Canon of Medicine.
Ibn Sina completed The Canon of Medicine around 1025.
Rhazes (al-Razi), a Persian physician who lived before Ibn Sina, wrote medical works that were studied in Europe.
